basis.cost: Static, cash, fiscal year, England and Wales, £ million; positive is a cost to the Exchequer
basis.distribution: Average change in household net income by equivalised household income decile, England and Wales, in the last policy year

measures.name: Raise the standard daily living rate (mock R6)
measures.description: Standard daily living £84.00 a week from April 2027, then CPI uprated and rounded to 5p.
measures.route_reason: A rate is a parameter; modelled directly.

measures.name: Raise the standard mobility rate (mock R7)
measures.description: Standard mobility £34.50 a week from April 2027 (corrected at 15:15), then CPI uprated and rounded to 5p.
measures.route_reason: A rate is a parameter; modelled directly.

measures.name: Hold the enhanced daily living rate in 2027-28 and 2028-29 (mock R10)
measures.description: Enhanced daily living held at £114.60 in 2027-28 and 2028-29 (corrected at 15:15); CPI uprating from April 2029 on £114.60, rounded to 5p.
measures.route_reason: A rate is a parameter; modelled directly.

measures.name: Enhanced daily living as the UC health element test (mock R11)
measures.description: From April 2029, only an enhanced daily living award (or the fast track) gives the UC health element.
measures.route_reason: Modelled by setting limited capability for work-related activity, for working-age people from 2029-30, to whether they hold an enhanced daily living award. The fast-track route is not modelled (no condition data); disability premiums in other benefits do not follow.

measures.name: Fluctuating conditions test (mock R1)
measures.route_reason: Acts through descriptors and the share of days they apply; the data hold awards, not points.

measures.name: Aids and appliances score 1 point (mock R2)
measures.route_reason: A points measure; the data hold awards, not points.

measures.name: Fast track for serious conditions (mock R3)
measures.route_reason: The data have no health-condition group to select people by.

measures.name: Ongoing awards for lifelong conditions (mock R4)
measures.route_reason: Changes flows on and off PIP over time; the model is static.

measures.name: PIP for 84 days in hospital (mock R5)
measures.route_reason: No hospital stays in the data or the model.

measures.name: Carer's Allowance for either component (mock R8)
measures.route_reason: Carer's Allowance in the model does not test the cared-for person's award, so carer effects are a ledger line.

measures.name: Independent advocacy service (mock R9)
measures.route_reason: Departmental spending on a service, not a benefit rule.

measures.name: Existing claimants at award review (mock R12)
measures.route_reason: A rule for how other measures apply; the assessment measures it phases are not computable.

measures.name: 52-week transitional protection (mock R13)
measures.route_reason: Protects award falls from the assessment measures, which are not computable; the model holds no review dates.

data_limits.reason: The data record each claimant's PIP daily living award (none, standard or enhanced), not assessment points, and a stored award overrides points. Changing a points threshold moves no one.
The data record each claimant's PIP mobility award, not assessment points, and a stored award overrides points. Changing a points threshold moves no one.

model_limits.reason: The model counts Scottish Adult Disability Payment and Northern Ireland PIP as PIP. Figures cover England and Wales households only.
Carer's Allowance in the model does not depend on the cared-for person's award, so a change to PIP awards leaves carers' payments unchanged.
The Universal Credit health element follows a recorded disability status, not PIP, so a change to PIP does not change it.
Recorded disability status does not follow a PIP change, so disability premiums and elements in other benefits stay the same.

The PIP caseload is calibrated to the OBR's PIP forecast for 2025-26, which is close to DWP's figures. In later years it grows with the population, not with DWP's caseload forecast, so it falls further below DWP's forecast in each later year.
